_doc: PULLBACK-HOLD-BULL-TRIGGER -- ITERATION 2, FROZEN pre-registration, written BEFORE any grid run. J-authorized 'replay til its tuned to work historically' -- this is the ONE permitted redesign; if v2 fails, the idea gets killed. Fixes EXACTLY the two structural failures diagnosed in v1 (see v1_root_cause below), nothing else. v1 files (detector, pre-reg, scorecard, stage summary) are left untouched as committed evidence -- this is a NEW dated pre-reg, not an edit to v1's.
supersedes: analysis/recommendations/pullback-hold-bull-prereg-2026-07-22.json (v1, NO_CELL_SHIPS -- kept as committed evidence, never edited)

v1_root_cause_being_fixed.failure_1_lagging_up_structure: v1's two up-structure qualifier candidates (MARKET_STRUCTURE trend, PRICE_VWAP) both read FALSE at J's own 2026-07-22 10:44-10:53 pullback-low bar (10:40 ET) and only recovered TRUE 15 min (PRICE_VWAP) / 45 min (MARKET_STRUCTURE) later -- both are lagging-confirmation signals by construction, so neither could ever see the entry J actually wanted live.
v1_root_cause_being_fixed.failure_2_loose_selectivity: v1's level-match rule accepted ANY LevelMemory level within the zone band, firing 9-13x/day (n=340-506 per cell on 39 days) -- diluting a distinctive, occasional J-named pattern into statistical noise (best cell: $1.60/trade expectancy, p=0.878, nowhere near BH-FDR significance).
v1_root_cause_being_fixed.fix_1: IMPULSE-LEG qualifier -- computable causally AT the pullback-low bar itself, no trend-confirmation lag, no VWAP-crossing lag. See detector_definition_space.up_structure_qualifier below.
v1_root_cause_being_fixed.fix_2: SELECTIVITY axis -- replaces any-level with either (a) a battle-tested (prior same-day touch) level or (b) a level that IS the impulse leg's own origin. Disclosed to cut entry frequency hard; see populations.disclosure and the replay tool's entries/day report.

up_structure_qualifier.name: IMPULSE-LEG
up_structure_qualifier.definition: Within the last K EXTENDED bars (premarket 04:00 ET onward + RTH, same calendar day) strictly BEFORE the candidate bar, there exists an upswing leg: leg_high = max(CLOSE) over that K-bar window; leg_origin_low = the LOW of the bar exactly K bars back (the window's own FIRST bar -- a fixed trailing reference, never a searched extremum, so a single low-liquidity premarket wick cannot be cherry-picked as the origin -- see hand_verification.origin_definition_rationale). leg_dollars = leg_high - leg_origin_low, must be >= M. The candidate bar's OWN low (pullback_low) must retrace <= R of that leg: (leg_high - pullback_low)/leg_dollars <= R. pullback_low must be STRICTLY ABOVE leg_origin_low (a genuine higher low, never an undercut).
up_structure_qualifier.evaluated_at: the pullback-low candidate bar itself (bar j), same convention as v1 -- a shallow pullback can transiently break intraday structure without invalidating the setup.
up_structure_qualifier.no_look_ahead: the K-bar window is strictly BEFORE the candidate bar's own extended-frame index; only the candidate bar's own low (never its close, never anything after it) is consulted 'in the present'. Guarded by test_pullback_hold_bull_v2.py's truncation test.

grid_axes_raw.note_full_factorial_not_used: K x M x R = 8 combinations; combined into 3 named IMPULSE_LEG_MODE presets (impulse_leg_mode axis below) to respect the <=36 cell cap, mirroring v1's own precedent of collapsing RSI-reset+green-close into one confirm_mode axis. M is FIXED at 1.00 (the looser value) across all 3 presets -- disclosed simplification: M never bound either anchor in hand-verification (leg_dollars was 2.60-3.37 at anchor_1, comfortably clearing both grid M values), so M is not the discriminating variable and was dropped from the swept axis to make room for K and R, which ARE discriminating (see hand_verification below).

impulse_leg_mode.rationale: Isolates one dimension change per preset from a common K24_M1.00_R0.786 baseline (the verified-passing combo): preset 2 tightens R only (tests the R-asymmetry the mission spec named explicitly); preset 3 shortens K only (tests whether a shorter lookback still captures a real leg). All 3 share M=1.00.

hand_verification._doc: Verified BEFORE this grid was run, against the ACTUAL cached backtest/data/spy_5m_2026-05-19_2026-07-22.csv bars (not synthetic) -- this is design-time pre-reg authoring (choosing K/M/R), not post-hoc tuning after seeing grid results; the grid itself is frozen below and not touched again after running.

K24_M1.00_R0.618.note: same leg, tighter R -- fails as expected, this IS the pre-registered asymmetry ('R=0.786 must pass it, R=0.618 will not; that asymmetry is expected and fine')

K12_M1.00_R0.786.note: pullback_low (746.76) < leg_origin_low (747.09) -- FAILS the 'higher low' condition outright, K=12's window is too short to reach behind the true launch point on this date

anchor_2_2026-07-21_bars_10:40_11:00_11:.note: all 3 impulse_leg_mode presets read TRUE at all three shelf-tap bars (retrace 0.42-0.56, well under even R=0.618) -- anchor_2's up-move is a much larger, cleaner leg than anchor_1's, so it is insensitive to the R/K choice within the grid. Full per-bar figures in the replay tool's diagnostic output.

hand_verification.origin_definition_rationale: A SEARCHED-extremum origin (min low anywhere in the K-window) was tried first and rejected: at K=24 it finds 2026-07-22 08:55 ET (low 744.30, volume 152,849 vs a typical premarket 5m bar of 10-50k -- a thin-liquidity wick), which manufactures leg_dollars=5.08 and retrace=0.516 -- LOW enough that even R=0.618 would pass, collapsing the R-grid's entire point as a selectivity axis. The fixed trailing-bar-K-back reference (leg_origin_low = low of the bar exactly K bars back) does not have this failure mode and is what is actually implemented.

selectivity.name: SELECTIVITY (replaces v1's any-LevelMemory-level rule)
candidates_considered: (a) PRIOR-INTERACTION: the matched level had >=1 same-day touch/bounce BEFORE the pullback candidate bar
(b) LEG-ORIGIN: the matched level IS (within zone_band_cents) the same bar's own impulse-leg origin low
selectivity.prior_interaction_impl: some bar strictly BEFORE the candidate bar (same day) had high/low within LevelMemory's own TOUCH_TOL (0.20, reused -- backtest.lib.watchers.level_memory.TOUCH_TOL) of the level price.
selectivity.leg_origin_impl: abs(level_price - leg_origin_low_at_candidate_bar) <= zone_band_cents (reused tolerance, not a new invented constant).
selectivity.disclosure: Both modes are pre-registered; a cell is NOT required to fire on every anchor to remain in the grid -- only the eventual SHIPPING cell must clear both sanity anchors (see ship_bar.cell_disqualified_if). Hand-verification found PRIOR_INTERACTION plausible at anchor_1 (LevelMemory's matched ~746.5x level shows a same-day touch at the 09:30 opening print, before the 10:40 pullback); LEG_ORIGIN was NOT expected to coincide with the LevelMemory-matched level at anchor_1 given the ~0.5 gap between the leg origin (746.01) and the matched level (~746.5x) -- disclosed here as an expected near-miss for that axis value at that anchor, not hidden after the fact.

zone_band_width.rule: UNCHANGED from v1 -- fixed-cents grid, symmetric zone [level - band, level + band].

hold_condition.rule: UNCHANGED from v1 -- pullback low enters the zone AND price closes back above zone_top within N bars of the pullback-low bar, checked over bars [j, j+N] inclusive.

confirmation_features.status: DROPPED in v2 (not part of the 4 frozen grid axes) -- disclosed simplification made to respect the <=36 cell cap once impulse_leg_mode (3) x selectivity_mode (2) are added; RSI-reset/green-close confirmation is entry-ENTRY tuning v1 already explored (all 18 confirm_mode=BOTH cells missed anchor_2 in v1) and is out of scope for this iteration, which is scoped to fix ONLY the two diagnosed structural failures.

exit_shape.base: IDENTICAL to v1 -- automation/state/fleet/strategies.py RIBBON_RIDE.exit (SS-B validated cell). Entry is the only thing being tuned in this iteration.
exit_shape.structure_stop_reference: trigger_level passed to walk_exit_manager = zone_low (level - band), IDENTICAL semantics to v1.

entry_pricing.strike: IDENTICAL to v1 -- ATM per live tier, crypto.lib.strike_selection.pick_strike via fleet_executor._tiers_for_arm on accounts.json arm 'safe-2'.
entry_pricing.qty: IDENTICAL to v1 -- min(params.json min_contracts=3, risk_gate.max_affordable_qty(...)).
entry_pricing.fill: IDENTICAL to v1 -- next 5-min OPRA option bar's VWAP at/after the entry bar's timestamp.
entry_pricing.exit_walk: IDENTICAL to v1 -- backtest.lib.exit_manager_walk.walk_exit_manager, the REAL production exit_manager decision core.

populations.full_history_source: backtest/data/spy_5m_2026-05-19_2026-07-22.csv -- SAME file as v1, but v2 loads it in TWO views: RTH-only (09:30-16:00, for entry/hold scanning, unchanged from v1) and EXTENDED (04:00-16:00, premarket-inclusive, NEW -- only feeds the impulse-leg qualifier's lookback).
populations.held_out_days_rule: IDENTICAL to v1 -- chronological tail, last 25% of opra_covered_days by date (round(39*0.25)=10), frozen here, never chosen after seeing results.
populations.disclosure: Detector-frequency stats (how often each cell fires, structurally, INCLUDING entries/day per cell -- the mission's explicit disclosure requirement given the selectivity axis is meant to cut frequency hard) are reported over the FULL 44-day history. Dollar P&L / expectancy / the ship gate are computed ONLY over the 39 OPRA-covered days (real option fills), per C1.

ship_bar._doc: IDENTICAL structure to v1 -- a cell only SHIPS if it clears ALL gates. Computed ONLY on the 39-day OPRA-covered real-fills population. IMMUTABLE per mission instruction -- copied verbatim from v1, not weakened.
ship_bar.condition_2_majority_of_covered_days_win: day-total P&L > 0 on a strict majority of days this cell produced >=1 real-fills entry
ship_bar.condition_3_survives_dropping_best_trade: total P&L minus the single largest-P&L trade is still > 0
ship_bar.condition_4_holds_on_held_out_subset: the held_out_days subset (last 10 OPRA days, never touched during tuning) has positive total P&L for this cell
ship_bar.condition_5_bh_fdr: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at q=0.10 across all 36 cells' one-sample significance test (mean P&L != 0) -- multiplicity correction across the whole grid, mandatory because 36 cells were tested.
ship_bar.cell_disqualified_if: the cell cannot produce a PULLBACK-HOLD entry event matching BOTH named sanity anchors below (fidelity check, evaluated BEFORE the ship-bar dollar gates) -- regardless of how good its aggregate P&L looks.
verdict_labels: NO_CELL_SHIPS (honest null -- report best near-miss + exact failed gate)

sanity_anchors._doc: IDENTICAL to v1's frozen anchors (unchanged windows/descriptions) -- fidelity checks, not P&L checks. A disqualifying cell fails regardless of aggregate.

anchor_1.description: higher-low ~746.80 over a known level_memory level ~746.54 (verified this fire: LevelMemory finds a support cluster at 746.59, memory_score 160, one bar prior to the low)
anchor_1.requirement: cell must emit >=1 PULLBACK-HOLD entry (reclaim/entry bar) with entry timestamp inside the window on this date

anchor_2.description: shelf 745.77-745.85 (three taps: 10:40 L745.77, 11:00 L745.83, 11:05 L745.85) then 11:15 CLOSE 747.41 above the 10:30/10:45 highs (verified this fire: LevelMemory finds a persistent support cluster ~745.60-745.89 across this window)
anchor_2.requirement: cell must emit >=1 PULLBACK-HOLD entry with entry timestamp inside the window on this date

no_post_hoc_tuning: The grid, populations, ship bar, and sanity anchors above are fixed at this file's write time. The replay tool may not adjust any of these after seeing results; a changed definition requires a new dated pre-reg (v3).
